title: Larval beetle jump — Laemophloeus biguttatus
citation: Bertone M.A. et al. (2022). A novel power-amplified jumping behavior in larval beetles (Coleoptera: Laemophloeidae). PLOS ONE 17(1): e0256509. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0256509 — video: S2 Video, shot 2.
licence: CC BY 4.0 (article and supplementary files) — video and data reused with attribution; overlays added by Pixels to Proof.
note: Our physics-based take-off speed (ballistic fit, validated by the gravity check) is about 7% above the value the authors obtained with a smoothing-spline method. The intervals overlap, so the verdict is REPRODUCED. On synthetic flights with known truth, the spline-peak method reads 3–10% low for slow, steep jumps — the likely cause of the gap (an inference, not a claim about the authors' error).
provenance: S1 Table row c_21382_488 (Larva9): velocity.max = 0.405 m/s, VelError = 0.059. VelError is a relative error in the authors' R script (ratio formula), so +/- = 0.059 x 0.405 = 0.024 m/s. That the video jump is jump 488 is an inference: take-off angle, distance, height and airborne time all match that row (74.6 deg, 9.44 mm, 8.64 mm, 0.081 s).
